3. Objective and optimizer health
Loss windows follow observed epoch cadence. Partial table-coverage epoch losses are retained in tables, without endpoint crosses. The selected receipt determines the included bases; a targeted TabPFN repair cohort does not imply missing TabICLv2 research runs. Numerical and clipping checks are tabulated; the shared schedule is shown once. Negative density NLL can be valid. Peak clipped fraction is the largest recorded epoch fraction, not the trial-wide fraction.

Figure: pd_pilot_loss_pd
PD data loss in recorded epochs, averaged within trial and update window before averaging trials. Window width is 13 updates, no finer than the typical epoch recording interval. Markers show observed windows; missing windows remain gaps. L2-SP is excluded. PD uses cross-entropy; LGD uses TabPFN bar-distribution NLL or TabICLv2 quantile pinball loss. Separate vertical scales preserve each model's loss evolution; their numerical magnitudes are not comparable. Epochs with incomplete table coverage are excluded from the curves and retained in the accompanying tables. Markers are thinned for readability; all recorded window means remain in the line and text summary.

Figure: lgd_pilot_loss_lgd
LGD data loss in recorded epochs, averaged within trial and update window before averaging trials. Window width is 6 updates, no finer than the typical epoch recording interval. Markers show observed windows; missing windows remain gaps. L2-SP is excluded. PD uses cross-entropy; LGD uses TabPFN bar-distribution NLL or TabICLv2 quantile pinball loss. Separate vertical scales preserve each model's loss evolution; their numerical magnitudes are not comparable. Epochs with incomplete table coverage are excluded from the curves and retained in the accompanying tables. Markers are thinned for readability; all recorded window means remain in the line and text summary.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

2. Credit transfer and non-credit retention
Historical objective provenance limits comparison with the corrected main grid. Missing milestones remain gaps; these pilots do not identify a universal optimum.

Figure: pd_budget_horizon_pd_updates
PD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

Figure: lgd_budget_horizon_lgd_updates
LGD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

3. Row exposure
The same milestone scores are plotted against cumulative processed row exposures, which include repeated observations.

Figure: pd_budget_horizon_pd_processed_rows
PD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

Figure: lgd_budget_horizon_lgd_processed_rows
LGD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

5. Objective, schedule and parameter movement
Losses retain separate architecture scales. Optimizer and parameter measurements are tabulated, and common learning-rate schedules share a figure.

Figure: pd_pilot_loss_pd
PD data loss in recorded epochs, averaged within trial and update window before averaging trials. Window width is 400 updates, no finer than the typical epoch recording interval. Markers show observed windows; missing windows remain gaps. L2-SP is excluded. PD uses cross-entropy; LGD uses TabPFN bar-distribution NLL or TabICLv2 quantile pinball loss. Separate vertical scales preserve each model's loss evolution; their numerical magnitudes are not comparable. Epochs with incomplete table coverage are excluded from the curves and retained in the accompanying tables. Markers are thinned for readability; all recorded window means remain in the line and text summary.

Figure: lgd_pilot_loss_lgd
LGD data loss in recorded epochs, averaged within trial and update window before averaging trials. Window width is 400 updates, no finer than the typical epoch recording interval. Markers show observed windows; missing windows remain gaps. L2-SP is excluded. PD uses cross-entropy; LGD uses TabPFN bar-distribution NLL or TabICLv2 quantile pinball loss. Separate vertical scales preserve each model's loss evolution; their numerical magnitudes are not comparable. Epochs with incomplete table coverage are excluded from the curves and retained in the accompanying tables. Markers are thinned for readability; all recorded window means remain in the line and text summary.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

Experiment 0: auxiliary experiment checks

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Project: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
These controls establish execution and measurement validity. They do not test whether credit-domain specialization improves generalization.

1. Planned checks
52 six-update arms across eight GPU tasks: 36 uninterrupted arms and 16 interrupted/resumed comparisons. LGD seed-42 one-sample also serves as the stratified sampling control. PD has a separate stratified control. The tiny 256-row cap and smoke retention panel bound debugging cost.

4. Final inference checks
This inference-only diagnostic uses two tables with observed numerical sensitivity and one control, not a new representative benchmark. Original, unchanged-save and CPT checkpoints use identical contexts and all test rows of five outer folds. The boundary probes use a fixed 256-row query subset in one fold and are reported separately. A passing parity check validates saving/reloading; differences between precision policies are measurements, not automatic failures. FP32 denotes tensor dtype with FA3 disabled; the recorded TF32 setting is also relevant.

Figure: pd_tabicl_numerical_policy
PD. TabICL five-fold AUC under automatic numerical settings and FP32 tensors with Flash Attention 3 disabled. The saved control writes unchanged original weights through the CPT serialization path. Contexts, preprocessing, inference views and test rows match between states and policies. The lower panel subtracts original from CPT AUC within policy and fold. Thin gray segments connect each of five paired fold effects; colored markers show their mean, not a confidence interval. The three post-hoc diagnostic tables were chosen to investigate observed numerical sensitivity and do not estimate its prevalence across credit tasks. Boundary probes are excluded from this figure.

6. Sampling and exposure illustration
Illustration only: a 10,000-row cap, all processed tables and no skipped updates. Actual runs use base-specific caps and training partitions.

Figure: planned_exposure_lgd_1
Illustrative optimizer-step shares using a 10,000-row batch cap, all registered processed tables and no skipped updates. One sample and accumulation share one marker because both assign one update per table visit; full pass assigns one per disjoint chunk. Dataset labels include row counts; the axis gives the total context-plus-query row cap per chunk. Multipliers beside full-pass dots give full-pass step share divided by equal-table step share, not the ratio of total update counts. Blue and red multiplier labels denote greater and smaller shares, respectively; these colors do not imply better or worse performance. Accumulation consumes all chunks whereas one sample consumes one; equal step shares therefore do not imply equal row exposure. Actual training uses the partition's training tables, base-specific caps and may stop mid-traversal.

## general/03_overview_pd

```
Overview: domain continued pretraining for PD

0. Evidence and interpretation
DATA: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Project: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Four research questions organize ten analyses. This overview shows the cross-study picture; rq1–rq4 contain the detailed training and benchmark evidence. Benefits depend on model, task and recipe, rather than being uniformly absent or positive.

1. Design, unique evidence and comparability
E1/E3/E4 reuse one 512-run factorial. E9 reuses E8’s exact large-table control. Counts use unique trial identities. Missing extensions and numerical-policy differences remain explicit.

2. Which models and recipes help?
All prescribed follow-up arms are shown alongside the predefined main reference and its frozen counterpart. No row is selected by its test outcome. Individual-table gains accompany corpus summaries in the RQ results notebooks.

Figure: pd_overview_outcomes
PD. For the predefined full/frozen reference and all prescribed follow-up arms, the share of held-out credit tables whose paired AUC change relative to the original model exceeds +0.1 percentage points (improved), lies within ±0.1 (negligible) or falls below −0.1 (worse); numbers give improved/total tables. The ±0.1 band is a reporting convention for this study, not a statistical equivalence margin. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight. The dotted line marks half of the tables.

PD. The predefined full-update reference (peak LR 3e-7, L2-SP 0.003, seed 42) on held-out credit tables. Horizontal values are ΔAUC (percentage points); vertical values are Brier reduction (×100). Each colored point represents one table with five complete paired outer folds for both metrics; the diamond is their equal-table mean. Both directions are oriented so that positive favors CPT. Axis ranges differ by base to retain small effects. AUC measures ranking; Brier score measures probability error, so their changes need not agree.

3. Transfer, retention and measured adaptation cost
Credit transfer and four-table non-credit retention are evaluated separately. Historical GPU-hours exclude queueing and benchmark inference; hardware/runtime differences limit timing comparisons. Adapter comparisons concern complete recipes.

Figure: pd_overview_transfer_retention
PD. Each point is one configuration: its equal-table mean paired change on held-out credit tables (horizontal) and on the four non-credit retention tables of the same task (vertical), both relative to the original model of the same base. Non-credit tables first average all four CPT training partitions. The upper-right quadrant improves both; the lower-right gains on credit while losing on the retention panel. Points outlined in black are the experiment-1 reference recipes (full and frozen). Axis limits differ between models. A four-table retention panel does not establish general retention. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight.

Each point is one configuration: its equal-table mean paired change in AUC (percentage points) on held-out credit tables against recorded training time summed over the four CPT partitions (logarithmic axis). Training time excludes evaluation and queueing and was recorded on the GPUs used for each study, so it is an observed cost, not a matched-compute comparison. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight.

Overview: domain continued pretraining for LGD

0. Evidence and interpretation
DATA: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Project: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Four research questions organize ten analyses. This overview shows the cross-study picture; rq1–rq4 contain the detailed training and benchmark evidence. Benefits depend on model, task and recipe, rather than being uniformly absent or positive.

1. Design, unique evidence and comparability
E1/E3/E4 reuse one 512-run factorial. E9 reuses E8’s exact large-table control. Counts use unique trial identities. Missing extensions and numerical-policy differences remain explicit.

2. Which models and recipes help?
All prescribed follow-up arms are shown alongside the predefined main reference and its frozen counterpart. No row is selected by its test outcome. Individual-table gains accompany corpus summaries in the RQ results notebooks.

Figure: lgd_overview_outcomes
LGD. For the predefined full/frozen reference and all prescribed follow-up arms, the share of held-out credit tables whose paired R² change relative to the original model exceeds +0.001  (improved), lies within ±0.001 (negligible) or falls below −0.001 (worse); numbers give improved/total tables. The ±0.001 band is a reporting convention for this study, not a statistical equivalence margin. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight. The dotted line marks half of the tables.

LGD. The predefined full-update reference (peak LR 3e-7, L2-SP 0.003, seed 42) on held-out credit tables. Horizontal values are ΔR²; vertical values are RMSE reduction (%). 3. Transfer, retention and measured adaptation cost
Credit transfer and four-table non-credit retention are evaluated separately. Historical GPU-hours exclude queueing and benchmark inference; hardware/runtime differences limit timing comparisons. Adapter comparisons concern complete recipes.

Figure: lgd_overview_transfer_retention
LGD. Each point is one configuration: its equal-table mean paired change on held-out credit tables (horizontal) and on the four non-credit retention tables of the same task (vertical), both relative to the original model of the same base. Non-credit tables first average all four CPT training partitions. The upper-right quadrant improves both; the lower-right gains on credit while losing on the retention panel. Points outlined in black are the experiment-1 reference recipes (full and frozen). Axis limits differ between models. A four-table retention panel does not establish general retention. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight.

Figure: lgd_overview_cost
LGD. Each point is one configuration: its equal-table mean paired change in R² on held-out credit tables against recorded training time summed over the four CPT partitions (logarithmic axis). Training time excludes evaluation and queueing and was recorded on the GPUs used for each study, so it is an observed cost, not a matched-compute comparison. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight.

4. Main findings and reading guide
Reference recipe, TabICLv2: mean -0.0055 R², median -0.0023, 1/8 tables improved, 5 worse (original 0.5319 → adapted 0.5264).
Reference recipe, TabPFN v2: mean +0.0041 R², median +0.0013, 4/8 tables improved, 2 worse (original 0.4745 → adapted 0.4786).
Reference recipe, TabPFN v2.6: mean -0.0832 R², median -0.0647, 1/8 tables improved, 7 worse (original 0.5398 → adapted 0.4566).
Reference recipe, TabPFN v3: mean -0.0284 R², median -0.0034, 1/8 tables improved, 7 worse (original 0.5394 → adapted 0.5110).
TabICLv2: 1 of 26 configurations have a mean gain above 0.001 R²; highest observed mean +0.0010 (Grid frozen · LR 3e-07 · λ 0), lowest -0.1683 (Grid all · LR 3e-05 · λ 0).
TabPFN v2: 11 of 26 configurations have a mean gain above 0.001 R²; highest observed mean +0.0058 (E7 Full pass), lowest -0.1323 (E6 LR 0.001).
TabPFN v2.6: 0 of 26 configurations have a mean gain above 0.001 R²; highest observed mean -0.0001 (Grid frozen · LR 3e-07 · λ 0.003), lowest -0.1861 (E5 LR 0.03).
TabPFN v3: 0 of 26 configurations have a mean gain above 0.001 R²; highest observed mean -0.0033 (E5 LR 0.0001), lowest -0.2536 (Grid all · LR 3e-05 · λ 0).
TabICLv2, shared factorial averaged over anchoring and scope: LR 3e-07 -0.0024, LR 1e-06 -0.0281, LR 1e-05 -0.0629, LR 3e-05 -0.0738 R².
TabPFN v2, shared factorial averaged over anchoring and scope: LR 3e-07 +0.0014, LR 1e-06 -0.0003, LR 1e-05 -0.0355, LR 3e-05 -0.0690 R².
TabPFN v2.6, shared factorial averaged over anchoring and scope: LR 3e-07 -0.0417, LR 1e-06 -0.0430, LR 1e-05 -0.0484, LR 3e-05 -0.0704 R².
TabPFN v3, shared factorial averaged over anchoring and scope: LR 3e-07 -0.0207, LR 1e-06 -0.0422, LR 1e-05 -0.1635, LR 3e-05 -0.2139 R².
RQ1 links learning rates with training-seed stability; RQ2 retains anchoring/freezing interactions and all adapter recipes; RQ3 separates sampling, corpus and episode effects; RQ4 shows original/CPT context curves and paired differences with fixed complete test rows. Numerical precision, table heterogeneity and overlapping training corpora bound the conclusions.

2. Learning rate, seed and training progress
E1 learning rates (full updates, L2-SP 0.003) and the E2 seed-43 repeat of the reference recipe share one view: query loss and fixed-context monitor changes on held-out credit and non-credit tables at the same successful-update milestones. Missing planned support remains a gap; native LGD loss scales differ between architectures. Two seeds are a limited stability check.

Figure: pd_trajectories
PD. Training trajectories by learning rate and seed. Rows show query loss, held-out credit, non-credit retention; columns show models. Query loss is the native training objective, averaged in successful-update windows with one contribution per planned trial; native LGD objectives differ across architectures and are compared only within a column. Monitor rows show changes from update zero on the fixed-context monitor, averaged over the same complete table and trial cohort at every milestone; they are training diagnostics, not five-fold benchmark results. Positive values favour CPT. The four training partitions contribute equally and shared controls appear once. Missing planned support is left as a gap. Equal update counts do not imply equal row exposure or compute.

Figure: lgd_trajectories
LGD. Training trajectories by learning rate and seed. Rows show query loss, held-out credit, non-credit retention; columns show models. Query loss is the native training objective, averaged in successful-update windows with one contribution per planned trial; native LGD objectives differ across architectures and are compared only within a column. Monitor rows show changes from update zero on the fixed-context monitor, averaged over the same complete table and trial cohort at every milestone; they are training diagnostics, not five-fold benchmark results. Positive values favour CPT. The four training partitions contribute equally and shared controls appear once. Missing planned support is left as a gap. Equal update counts do not imply equal row exposure or compute.

4. Applied learning-rate schedules and scope
The applied schedule follows the declared update horizon. Rate comparisons do not change the budget, and repeated controls are not additional replications. Missing follow-up outputs require the completed campaign download, not a zero-effect interpretation.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

RQ1: transfer and stability — final results

0. Evidence and interpretation
DATA: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Project: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
E1 learning rates and E2 training seeds are viewed together. E1 keeps full updates with L2-SP 0.003; RQ2 retains the complete factorial. Final evaluation averages five paired outer folds within table, then weights tables equally. AUC/R² gains are CPT minus original; Brier/RMSE gains reverse direction. RMSE gains here are relative percentages.

2. Original-to-CPT effects across the research question
Held-out credit transfer (primary and secondary metric) and non-credit retention share one view. Every dot is a table, the diamond is the equal-table mean and the bar is the table interquartile range: heterogeneity, not a confidence interval. The same tables contribute to every displayed recipe within each model and column.

Figure: pd_effects
PD. Transfer and retention by learning rate and seed. Each CPT recipe is compared with its own original model; positive values favour CPT. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight. Within a model and column, every displayed recipe uses the same tables; cohorts can differ between models and columns. Retention values first average the four training partitions. Horizontal axes are scaled per panel. Absent rows were not run for that model; they are not zero effects.

Figure: lgd_effects
LGD. Transfer and retention by learning rate and seed. Each CPT recipe is compared with its own original model; positive values favour CPT. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight. Within a model and column, every displayed recipe uses the same tables; cohorts can differ between models and columns. Retention values first average the four training partitions. Horizontal axes are scaled per panel. Absent rows were not run for that model; they are not zero effects.

5. The fixed reference: named tables and prediction quality
The reference is fixed independently of held-out outcomes. Named-table plots and saved-prediction diagnostics show whether the mean hides heterogeneity. Signed residuals are not the theoretical model bias; table-bootstrap intervals are conditional on these fitted checkpoints.

Figure: pd_reference_tables
PD. Experiment 1, predefined reference recipe (all trainable weights updated, peak LR 3e-7, L2-SP λ 0.003, seed 42), final five-fold benchmark: paired change in AUC (percentage points) on every held-out credit table relative to the original model of the same base. Each axis label gives the equal-table mean and the number of tables improving by more than 0.1 pp. Filled markers: at least four of the five outer folds change in the direction of the table mean; open markers: the folds disagree. Tables are ordered by their mean effect across the four bases; horizontal axes differ between models. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight.

PD. Mean paired benchmark effects of the predefined full-update CPT reference and 95% conditional table-bootstrap intervals. Figure: pd_calibration_overview
PD. Changes in the displayed outer-test probability-quality scores for the predefined full-update reference (LR 3e-7, L2-SP 0.003, one-sample training) relative to its untuned base. Positive reductions favor continued pretraining (CPT). Raw probabilities and validation-fitted Platt and isotonic calibration use a common dataset cohort within each base: all 9 scores require the same five completed, matched outer folds. Diamonds show equal-dataset means; horizontal lines span dataset quartiles, not confidence intervals. Log loss, when exported, is in nats; ECE depends on the binning scheme.

Figure: lgd_reference_tables
LGD. Experiment 1, predefined reference recipe (all trainable weights updated, peak LR 3e-7, L2-SP λ 0.003, seed 42), final five-fold benchmark: paired change in R² on every held-out credit table relative to the original model of the same base. Each axis label gives the equal-table mean and the number of tables improving by more than 0.001 R². Filled markers: at least four of the five outer folds change in the direction of the table mean; open markers: the folds disagree. Tables are ordered by their mean effect across the four bases; horizontal axes differ between models. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight.

Figure: lgd_reference_uncertainty
LGD. Mean paired benchmark effects of the predefined full-update CPT reference and 95% conditional table-bootstrap intervals. Positive effects favor CPT; RMSE is reported as fractional error reduction. Filled circles include all credit tables; open squares retain documented public sources. Each table contributes the mean of five paired outer folds. Source restriction is based on provenance, not scores. Intervals do not capture training-seed uncertainty or establish source independence.

Figure: lgd_prediction_diagnostics
LGD. Matched five-fold out-of-fold predictions on held-out credit tables. Circles show individual tables; their small vertical offsets follow table-name order and have no quantitative meaning. Black diamonds are equal-table means; segments are dataset interquartile ranges, not confidence intervals. Each label gives the number of tables. Mean error is predicted minus observed target, pooled over test rows within a table. The left panel measures reduction of its absolute value; the right measures reduction in squared error. These are empirical errors, not a theoretical bias–variance decomposition.

Figure: lgd_factor_training
LGD. Monitor change of the alternative choice minus its reference after matching the learning rate and the other factor, on held-out credit (top) and non-credit retention (bottom); positive values mean the alternative transfers or retains more. Recipes are averaged within table, then tables equally; missing planned support stays missing. Both factors come from the same 512-run factorial; its four cells and their interaction are reported with the final benchmark.

3. DiagScale and LoRA recipe dynamics
Both adapter studies at every prescribed rate: query loss and fixed-context monitor changes on held-out credit and non-credit tables. Within-model objectives and monitor changes are descriptive; no difference is attributed solely to the adapter mechanism.

Figure: pd_adapter_trajectories
PD. Adapter training trajectories by recipe. Rows show query loss, held-out credit, non-credit retention; columns show models. Query loss is the native training objective, averaged in successful-update windows with one contribution per planned trial; native LGD objectives differ across architectures and are compared only within a column. Monitor rows show changes from update zero on the fixed-context monitor, averaged over the same complete table and trial cohort at every milestone; they are training diagnostics, not five-fold benchmark results. Positive values favour CPT. The four training partitions contribute equally and shared controls appear once. Missing planned support is left as a gap. Equal update counts do not imply equal row exposure or compute.

Figure: lgd_adapter_trajectories
LGD. Adapter training trajectories by recipe. Rows show query loss, held-out credit, non-credit retention; columns show models. Query loss is the native training objective, averaged in successful-update windows with one contribution per planned trial; native LGD objectives differ across architectures and are compared only within a column. Monitor rows show changes from update zero on the fixed-context monitor, averaged over the same complete table and trial cohort at every milestone; they are training diagnostics, not five-fold benchmark results. Positive values favour CPT. The four training partitions contribute equally and shared controls appear once. Missing planned support is left as a gap. Equal update counts do not imply equal row exposure or compute.

RQ2: restricted updates — final results

0. Evidence and interpretation
DATA: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Project: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
E3 anchoring and E4 freezing reuse one factorial. E5 DiagScale and E6 LoRA are specified recipes with different sampling, episode sizes, precision and regularization; they do not isolate adapter mechanisms. Final evaluation averages five paired outer folds within table, then weights tables equally. AUC/R² gains are CPT minus original; Brier/RMSE gains reverse direction. RMSE gains here are relative percentages.

1. Coverage, protocols and unique evidence
Training completion and benchmark completion are separate. All results retain their own matched original checkpoint. The current inference-policy table governs cross-study TabICL comparisons; a pending FP32 refresh is not published evidence.

2. The complete anchoring × freezing factorial
All four full/frozen × unanchored/anchored cells at every learning rate, for both credit metrics and non-credit retention. Anchoring and freezing simple effects and their interaction remain in the numerical record. Positive changes relative to the original differ from merely reducing degradation.

Figure: pd_factorial
PD. Equal-table mean CPT-minus-original effect of each cell of the full/frozen × unanchored/anchored factorial (E3 anchoring, E4 freezing) at every peak learning rate; positive values favour CPT. Within a model and row, all four cells and all learning rates use one complete table cohort. Five folds are averaged within table; retention first averages the four training partitions. Simple effects and the difference-in-differences interaction are retained in the text summary. E1, E3 and E4 reuse one 512-run campaign; they are not independent repetitions.

Figure: lgd_factorial
LGD. Equal-table mean CPT-minus-original effect of each cell of the full/frozen × unanchored/anchored factorial (E3 anchoring, E4 freezing) at every peak learning rate; positive values favour CPT. Within a model and row, all four cells and all learning rates use one complete table cohort. Five folds are averaged within table; retention first averages the four training partitions. Simple effects and the difference-in-differences interaction are retained in the text summary. E1, E3 and E4 reuse one 512-run campaign; they are not independent repetitions.
Held-out credit R²: all four paired cell values

3. Adapter recipes and the predefined full-update reference
DiagScale and LoRA appear at all prescribed rates beside the predefined full-update reference, for both credit metrics and non-credit retention, on a fixed table cohort per model and column. The recipes differ in more than the adapter; no mechanism ranking follows from this comparison.

Figure: pd_effects
PD. Adapter recipes against the full-update reference. Each CPT recipe is compared with its own original model; positive values favour CPT. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight. Within a model and column, every displayed recipe uses the same tables; cohorts can differ between models and columns. Retention values first average the four training partitions. Horizontal axes are scaled per panel. Absent rows were not run for that model; they are not zero effects. Models without at least two comparable recipes are omitted.

Figure: lgd_effects
LGD. Adapter recipes against the full-update reference. Each CPT recipe is compared with its own original model; positive values favour CPT. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight. Within a model and column, every displayed recipe uses the same tables; cohorts can differ between models and columns. Retention values first average the four training partitions. Horizontal axes are scaled per panel. Absent rows were not run for that model; they are not zero effects. Models without at least two comparable recipes are omitted.

2. Sampling, corpus and episode trajectories
E7 sampling and the E8/E9 corpus and episode-size arms are shown in separate figures to preserve their interpretation. The large-table 8,192-row curve is the shared E8/E9 control. Monitor rows describe fixed-context monitoring on excluded tables.

Figure: pd_sampling_trajectories
PD. Training trajectories by sampling policy. Rows show query loss, held-out credit, non-credit retention; columns show models. Query loss is the native training objective, averaged in successful-update windows with one contribution per planned trial; native LGD objectives differ across architectures and are compared only within a column. Monitor rows show changes from update zero on the fixed-context monitor, averaged over the same complete table and trial cohort at every milestone; they are training diagnostics, not five-fold benchmark results. Positive values favour CPT. The four training partitions contribute equally and shared controls appear once. Missing planned support is left as a gap. Equal update counts do not imply equal row exposure or compute.

Figure: pd_corpus_episode_trajectories
PD. Training trajectories by corpus and episode size. Rows show query loss, held-out credit, non-credit retention; columns show models. Query loss is the native training objective, averaged in successful-update windows with one contribution per planned trial; native LGD objectives differ across architectures and are compared only within a column. Monitor rows show changes from update zero on the fixed-context monitor, averaged over the same complete table and trial cohort at every milestone; they are training diagnostics, not five-fold benchmark results. Positive values favour CPT. The four training partitions contribute equally and shared controls appear once. Missing planned support is left as a gap. Equal update counts do not imply equal row exposure or compute.

Figure: lgd_sampling_trajectories
LGD. Training trajectories by sampling policy. Rows show query loss, held-out credit, non-credit retention; columns show models. Query loss is the native training objective, averaged in successful-update windows with one contribution per planned trial; native LGD objectives differ across architectures and are compared only within a column. Monitor rows show changes from update zero on the fixed-context monitor, averaged over the same complete table and trial cohort at every milestone; they are training diagnostics, not five-fold benchmark results. Positive values favour CPT. The four training partitions contribute equally and shared controls appear once. Missing planned support is left as a gap. Equal update counts do not imply equal row exposure or compute.

3. Exposure is different from update count
The same sampling curves are indexed by processed row exposures, including repeated rows. This reveals the additional data and computation behind a fixed update budget; it is not a unique-row count.

Figure: pd_sampling_exposure
PD. Monitor changes per processed row exposure. Rows show held-out credit, non-credit retention; columns show models. Monitor rows show changes from update zero on the fixed-context monitor, averaged over the same complete table and trial cohort at every milestone; they are training diagnostics, not five-fold benchmark results. Positive values favour CPT. The four training partitions contribute equally and shared controls appear once. Missing planned support is left as a gap. Rows seen count repeated observations, on a logarithmic axis; equal updates do not imply equal rows or compute.

Figure: lgd_sampling_exposure
LGD. Monitor changes per processed row exposure. Rows show held-out credit, non-credit retention; columns show models. Monitor rows show changes from update zero on the fixed-context monitor, averaged over the same complete table and trial cohort at every milestone; they are training diagnostics, not five-fold benchmark results. Positive values favour CPT. The four training partitions contribute equally and shared controls appear once. Missing planned support is left as a gap. Rows seen count repeated observations, on a logarithmic axis; equal updates do not imply equal rows or compute.

RQ3: training data and exposure — final results

0. Evidence and interpretation
DATA: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Project: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
E7 sampling, E8 corpus eligibility and E9 episode size address distinct changes in data exposure. E8/E9 are PD-only. The exact large-table 8,192-row control is reused once. Equal optimizer updates do not imply equal compute or unique rows. Final evaluation averages five paired outer folds within table, then weights tables equally. AUC/R² gains are CPT minus original; Brier/RMSE gains reverse direction. RMSE gains here are relative percentages.

1. Coverage, protocols and unique evidence
Training completion and benchmark completion are separate. All results retain their own matched original checkpoint. The current inference-policy table governs cross-study TabICL comparisons; a pending FP32 refresh is not published evidence.

2. Original-to-CPT effects across the research question
Held-out credit transfer (primary and secondary metric) and non-credit retention share one view. Every dot is a table, the diamond is the equal-table mean and the bar is the table interquartile range: heterogeneity, not a confidence interval. The same tables contribute to every displayed recipe within each model and column.

Figure: pd_effects
PD. Transfer and retention by training-data choice. Each CPT recipe is compared with its own original model; positive values favour CPT. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight. Within a model and column, every displayed recipe uses the same tables; cohorts can differ between models and columns. Retention values first average the four training partitions. Horizontal axes are scaled per panel. Absent rows were not run for that model; they are not zero effects.

Figure: lgd_effects
LGD. Transfer and retention by training-data choice. Each CPT recipe is compared with its own original model; positive values favour CPT. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight. Within a model and column, every displayed recipe uses the same tables; cohorts can differ between models and columns. Retention values first average the four training partitions. Horizontal axes are scaled per panel. Absent rows were not run for that model; they are not zero effects.

Figure: pd_choices
PD. Paired differences between planned data choices. Each value is the difference between two recipes' CPT-minus-original effects on the same table and model; positive favours the recipe named first and can mean less degradation rather than positive transfer. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight. Within a model and column, every displayed recipe uses the same tables; cohorts can differ between models and columns. Retention values first average the four training partitions. Horizontal axes are scaled per panel. Absent rows were not run for that model; they are not zero effects.

Figure: lgd_choices
LGD. Paired differences between planned data choices. Each value is the difference between two recipes' CPT-minus-original effects on the same table and model; positive favours the recipe named first and can mean less degradation rather than positive transfer. Each adapted model is paired with its own original checkpoint on the same split and outer fold; five folds are averaged within table and tables receive equal weight. Within a model and column, every displayed recipe uses the same tables; cohorts can differ between models and columns. Retention values first average the four training partitions. Horizontal axes are scaled per panel. Absent rows were not run for that model; they are not zero effects.

## rq4/01_context_curves

```
RQ4 (E10): labeled context and the value of CPT

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Project: output CreditPFN; modified 2026-11-03T14:42:13+00:00; read only.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Does credit CPT change the value of labeled context on an excluded credit table? Dependence on context size is different from variability across repeated contexts of the same size.

1. Fixed checkpoints and evaluation protocol
The 50,000-row cap bounds computation; it is not TabPFN v3’s native limit. The available-pool endpoint is included when distinct. Validation and test rows never enter context.

Table: Evaluation protocol
CSV (first column: row index)
row,setting,value

2,Dataset exclusion,Each table uses its original experiment-1 held-out partition's checkpoint
3,Outer test folds,5
4,Context rows,"8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048, 3072, 4096, 6144, 8192, 12288, 16384, 20480, 24576, 32768, 40960, 49152, 50000"

3. Original and CPT context curves
Panels show PD AUC/Brier and LGD R²/RMSE, with original and CPT levels and improvement-oriented paired differences. Scores first average the five paired folds within each table, then weight tables equally. Positive differences favor CPT. Individual table curves reveal opposing responses or influential tables that a mean can hide; the same table identities persist across each horizon. No figure is generated for a horizon without a complete common cohort.

Figure: context_pd
Top: equal-table mean AUC of the original model and the fixed-recipe CPT checkpoint as labelled context grows. Middle and bottom: paired CPT effects for the primary and secondary metric; positive values favour CPT, thin curves are individual tables and thick curves their equal-table mean. Each column fixes one table cohort across every context size and both models, so levels need not agree between columns. Scores average five paired outer folds within table before tables receive equal weight; curves are not uncertainty bands. Validation labels use a separate fixed budget and all outer-test rows are unchanged. The CPT checkpoint is the E1 reference recipe (full updates, LR 3×10⁻⁷, L2-SP 0.003) trained on a partition that excluded the table.

Figure: context_lgd
Top: equal-table mean R² of the original model and the fixed-recipe CPT checkpoint as labelled context grows. Middle and bottom: paired CPT effects for the primary and secondary metric; positive values favour CPT, thin curves are individual tables and thick curves their equal-table mean. Each column fixes one table cohort across every context size and both models, so levels need not agree between columns. Scores average five paired outer folds within table before tables receive equal weight; curves are not uncertainty bands. Validation labels use a separate fixed budget and all outer-test rows are unchanged. The CPT checkpoint is the E1 reference recipe (full updates, LR 3×10⁻⁷, L2-SP 0.003) trained on a partition that excluded the table.

Figure: context_pd_tables
Paired CPT effect, averaged over five outer folds, for every held-out credit table (rows, ordered by available context) and nominal context size (columns); blue favours CPT and red the original model. Rows show the primary metric (top) and secondary metric (bottom). Colour limits are symmetric at the 95th percentile of absolute effects per metric and extreme cells saturate; printed values are exact. Grey cells exceed the table's available training rows. Each table keeps its fold membership, nested context subsets and complete test rows at every size.

Figure: context_lgd_tables
Paired CPT effect, averaged over five outer folds, for every held-out credit table (rows, ordered by available context) and nominal context size (columns); blue favours CPT and red the original model. Rows show the primary metric (top) and secondary metric (bottom). Colour limits are symmetric at the 95th percentile of absolute effects per metric and extreme cells saturate; printed values are exact. Grey cells exceed the table's available training rows. Each table keeps its fold membership, nested context subsets and complete test rows at every size.

Fold averages are descriptive, not independent table replications.

Additional TabPFN v2 and v2.6 coverage
Extension study20261030d. This model-coverage extension was added after inspecting the original study; it is exploratory. The original tables and partitions are preserved. Experiment 10 caps inference context at 10,000 rows for TabPFN v2 and 50,000 for v2.6. Experiment 9 uses 2,048, the shared 8,192-row control, and the model-specific training ceiling (10,000 or 11,000 total context-plus-query rows). Missing evidence is not a zero effect.

Figure: extension_study20261030d_v2_context_pd
TabPFN v2. Top: equal-table mean AUC of the original model and the fixed-recipe CPT checkpoint as labelled context grows. Middle and bottom: paired CPT effects for the primary and secondary metric; positive values favour CPT, thin curves are individual tables and thick curves their equal-table mean. Each column fixes one table cohort across every context size and both models, so levels need not agree between columns. Scores average five paired outer folds within table before tables receive equal weight; curves are not uncertainty bands. Validation labels use a separate fixed budget and all outer-test rows are unchanged. The CPT checkpoint is the E1 reference recipe (full updates, LR 3×10⁻⁷, L2-SP 0.003) trained on a partition that excluded the table.

Figure: extension_study20261030d_v2_context_lgd
TabPFN v2. Top: equal-table mean R² of the original model and the fixed-recipe CPT checkpoint as labelled context grows. Middle and bottom: paired CPT effects for the primary and secondary metric; positive values favour CPT, thin curves are individual tables and thick curves their equal-table mean. Each column fixes one table cohort across every context size and both models, so levels need not agree between columns. Scores average five paired outer folds within table before tables receive equal weight; curves are not uncertainty bands. Validation labels use a separate fixed budget and all outer-test rows are unchanged. The CPT checkpoint is the E1 reference recipe (full updates, LR 3×10⁻⁷, L2-SP 0.003) trained on a partition that excluded the table.

TabPFN v2. Rows show the primary metric (top) and secondary metric (bottom). Colour limits are symmetric at the 95th percentile of absolute effects per metric and extreme cells saturate; printed values are exact. Grey cells exceed the table's available training rows. Each table keeps its fold membership, nested context subsets and complete test rows at every size.

TabPFN v2. Paired CPT effect, averaged over five outer folds, for every held-out credit table (rows, ordered by available context) and nominal context size (columns); blue favours CPT and red the original model. Rows show the primary metric (top) and secondary metric (bottom). Colour limits are symmetric at the 95th percentile of absolute effects per metric and extreme cells saturate; printed values are exact. Grey cells exceed the table's available training rows. Each table keeps its fold membership, nested context subsets and complete test rows at every size.

Figure: extension_study20261030d_v2p6_context_pd
TabPFN v2.6. Top: equal-table mean AUC of the original model and the fixed-recipe CPT checkpoint as labelled context grows. Middle and bottom: paired CPT effects for the primary and secondary metric; positive values favour CPT, thin curves are individual tables and thick curves their equal-table mean. Each column fixes one table cohort across every context size and both models, so levels need not agree between columns. Scores average five paired outer folds within table before tables receive equal weight; curves are not uncertainty bands. Validation labels use a separate fixed budget and all outer-test rows are unchanged. The CPT checkpoint is the E1 reference recipe (full updates, LR 3×10⁻⁷, L2-SP 0.003) trained on a partition that excluded the table.

Figure: extension_study20261030d_v2p6_context_lgd
TabPFN v2.6. Top: equal-table mean R² of the original model and the fixed-recipe CPT checkpoint as labelled context grows. Middle and bottom: paired CPT effects for the primary and secondary metric; positive values favour CPT, thin curves are individual tables and thick curves their equal-table mean. Each column fixes one table cohort across every context size and both models, so levels need not agree between columns. Scores average five paired outer folds within table before tables receive equal weight; curves are not uncertainty bands. Validation labels use a separate fixed budget and all outer-test rows are unchanged. The CPT checkpoint is the E1 reference recipe (full updates, LR 3×10⁻⁷, L2-SP 0.003) trained on a partition that excluded the table.

TabPFN v2.6. Paired CPT effect, averaged over five outer folds, for every held-out credit table (rows, ordered by available context) and nominal context size (columns); blue favours CPT and red the original model. Rows show the primary metric (top) and secondary metric (bottom). Colour limits are symmetric at the 95th percentile of absolute effects per metric and extreme cells saturate; printed values are exact. Grey cells exceed the table's available training rows. Each table keeps its fold membership, nested context subsets and complete test rows at every size.

TabPFN v2.6. Paired CPT effect, averaged over five outer folds, for every held-out credit table (rows, ordered by available context) and nominal context size (columns); blue favours CPT and red the original model. Rows show the primary metric (top) and secondary metric (bottom). Colour limits are symmetric at the 95th percentile of absolute effects per metric and extreme cells saturate; printed values are exact. Grey cells exceed the table's available training rows. Each table keeps its fold membership, nested context subsets and complete test rows at every size.
